_doc.what: Expected statistics of frametimes.csv. Scripts/test_gauntlet_model.py checks QuebecGauntletModel.h against it, and the Python gauntlet metrics use the same pair.
_doc.csv: frametimes.csv has a header row and the columns frame_ms (milliseconds, 3 decimals) and leg (a leg name such as S1-S2). Rows are in frame order. Every row belongs to a measured leg; there are no warm-up or hold rows.
_doc.percentile: sorted(values)[ceil((n - 1) * fraction)], the rule of Scripts/profile_package.py. p50_ms uses the same rule, not the mean of the two middle values.
_doc.counts: over_33_3ms, over_50ms, over_66_7ms and over_250ms count frames strictly over 33.3, 50, 66.7 and 250 ms. The CSV has frames exactly at each limit, which do not count.
_doc.seconds: Sum of frame_ms in row order, divided by 1000, rounded to 6 decimals. Compare it within 1e-6 s (QuebecGauntletModel.h prints 3 decimals, so that comparison uses 5e-4 s).
_doc.legs: Rows of each leg, in drive order.
